surprises.head: A shutout for Connor Hellebuyck
surprises.body: Hellebuyck stopped all 23 shots, worth 1.9 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 10 starts.

story.head: Hellebuyck slams the door on the Maple Leafs
paras: Timo Meier struck first for the Devils midway through the second, with Nico Hischier picking up his 500th NHL point on the goal. He scored his second of the night a little over four minutes later to make it 2-0. The Maple Leafs’ Colton Sissons left late in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. Hischier extended the lead to 3-0 on the power play midway through the third, and Connor Brown added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 4-0.

The chances were closer than the score. Connor Hellebuyck was perfect for the Devils, 23 saves on 23 shots, and Anthony Stolarz stopped 25 of 28 at the other end. Hellebuyck has won all five of his starts this season, matching Craig Billington (1991-92), Chris Terreri (1993-94), Akira Schmid (2022-23) and Jake Allen (2025-26) for the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history.
A scrum in the final minutes sent four players to the box. The Devils moved to 13-5-0, second in the Metropolitan, while the Maple Leafs dropped to 8-9-2, seventh in the Atlantic.
